pages.text: A snack boat with a green awning glided up. Bung took a bag. Little Ddori watched. "Only one!"
"Mom, a big bowl full of noodles at dinner!" Mom smiled and nodded. The tied boat rocked once in the snack boat's wake.
The ice boat passed, then a fruit boat. Bung reached again. An empty snack bag and melted-ice marks lay on the floor.
Lights came on. Mom served dinner noodles, but Bung's tummy was full. Ddori had already eaten half. "I cannot eat noodles..."
Mom sat close, gently circling a hand on that full tummy. "Three boats passed today, right?" Bung lowered the head. "But I want noodles..."
"Your tummy has room too. Fill it all, and noodles have nowhere to go. Just one snack boat!" Mom cupped her hands. Bung raised one finger.
Next afternoon, Bung took only one bag from the snack boat and rested both hands on the knees. When the ice boat passed, the hands stayed put.
At dinner, Bung's tummy rumbled. One whole noodle bowl, gone! "Wow! Were noodles always this tasty?"
A fruit boat passed close. Bung drew Ddori's hand close; the other stayed on the knee. "One, just one snack boat! Two, noodles first! Three, hands down for the others!"
Mom hugged Bung in both arms. Fewer snacks made dinner noodles tastier. Bung shared a snack piece with Ddori. "Just one snack boat!"
